advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the byte-accurate guard to also cover quoted-string alarm_descriptions (or convert the existing char-based test to measure UTF-8 bytes), so no description form is measured in the wrong unit.
evidence: tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py:516: `if len(rendered) > _AWS_ALARM_DESCRIPTION_MAX:` measures characters, not UTF-8 bytes
tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py:498 docstring: 'stays under AWS's 1024-character cap' -- wrong unit, the defect the ticket documents

New test only matches heredocs: `_ALARM_DESCRIPTION_RE` requires `<<(?P<dedent>-?)...` (tests/unit/test_alarm_description_byte_limit.py:22-26); quoted-form descriptions return None at line 104-105 and are dropped at line 123
tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py:464-467 notes the quoted form is used by three real alarms in monitoring.tf
advisory.finding: The pre-existing guard test_alarm_descriptions_fit_the_aws_limit measures description length in Python CHARACTERS (len(rendered)), which is the exact units defect this ticket fixes; the new byte-accurate guard only covers heredoc descriptions, so the three quoted-string alarm_descriptions (the two EC2 status-check alarms and gerrit_data_disk_high) remain guarded ONLY by the character-unit test and would pass a byte-over-limit value if they ever gained multibyte characters.
scenarios: A future quoted-string alarm_description gains a multibyte character (em dash, curly quote) that pushes it from <=1024 chars to >1024 bytes: the new heredoc-only test skips it and the old test counts it as characters, so terraform plan breaks again exactly as in this bug.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a quoted-form branch to the new test (or fold the byte check into the existing test that already handles both forms) so every alarm_description, heredoc or quoted, is measured in UTF-8 bytes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a parser correctness test: feed a synthetic alarm block whose dedented UTF-8 body is >1024 bytes (and one at exactly 1024) and assert _alarm_descriptions/_description_from_block reports the over-limit one as an offender and the boundary one as compliant.
evidence: tests/unit/test_alarm_description_byte_limit.py:129-133 — test_parser_finds_the_alarm_descriptions_it_guards only asserts `len(descriptions) >= _MIN_EXPECTED_ALARM_DESCRIPTIONS` (34); it does not verify the measured byte_count of any description.

tests/unit/test_alarm_description_byte_limit.py:142-144 — the offender check `if description.byte_count > _ALARM_DESCRIPTION_BYTE_LIMIT` trusts byte_count, but no test drives _description_from_block/_dedent_indented_heredoc with an input whose rendered byte length is known to exceed 1024 to prove an offender IS flagged.

ABSENCE: no test constructs a synthetic alarm block (e.g. a heredoc whose dedented UTF-8 body is exactly 1025 bytes, or one using em dashes) and asserts _alarm_descriptions()/_description_from_block reports it as an offender.
tests/unit/test_alarm_description_byte_limit.py:130 — guard is a bare count `>= 34`, not a membership check on resource_name.
tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py:244 — a sibling test deliberately PINS `docker_buildkit_cache_high` by name for the same file; this new guard does not.
ABSENCE: no assertion that `docker_buildkit_cache_high` (the alarm the diff edits) appears in _alarm_descriptions() resource names.
advisory.finding: The parser's byte-measurement path (dedent application + UTF-8 encoding), which is the load-bearing new logic, is never verified against a controlled synthetic description of known byte length; the offender test can pass vacuously if _dedent_indented_heredoc or the newline/terminator handling under-counts bytes, defeating the exact regression the change targets (a description at 1025 rendered bytes).
merged_from: No test pins that the specific alarm changed by this diff (docker_buildkit_cache_high) is actually among the parsed descriptions; the count>=34 guard can be satisfied by other alarms, so a parser change that silently drops this heredoc would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add table-driven cases exercising _description_from_block on inline strings: one heredoc body dedenting to exactly 1024 bytes (compliant) and one to 1025 bytes and one containing em dashes (flagged), asserting AlarmDescription.byte_count and the offender predicate directly — independent of the real .tf files.
